llm.summary: The skill is coherent for Outlit customer intelligence, but needs review because its setup instructions recommend running a downloaded installer directly in the shell.

dimensions.detail: Use of Outlit API keys, OAuth, stored CLI credentials, and sensitive customer/business data is proportionate to the product purpose and is documented with grant boundaries and least-privilege guidance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact includes `curl -fsSL https://outlit.ai/install.sh | bash`, which executes remote code without a separate inspection or verification step, although the manifest and text also provide safer npm and Homebrew options.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger scope is broad but bounded to Outlit interfaces and workspace data, with explicit exclusions for generic customer-success advice and instructions to perform write operations only when the user explicitly asks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill describes credential resolution, browser login, MCP OAuth, and setup commands, but I found no hidden persistence, background service, privilege escalation, or instruction to bypass permissions; merge execution is explicitly gated and defaults to preview.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s read and write capabilities fit its stated Outlit purpose, including customer intelligence, SQL analytics, access management, integrations, activation, settings, features, and identity merges; the high-impact workspace actions are disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Prefer installing with npm or Homebrew instead of the curl-to-bash command unless you have independently verified and trust the installer. Use least-privilege Outlit credentials, avoid pasting secrets into chat, and review any requested workspace changes carefully, especially access changes, integration setup, and customer merges.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: Accepted as a material review concern: installing a CLI is purpose-aligned, but the documented curl-to-bash path executes network-fetched code without verification.
[TM2] expected: Accepted as the same install-path concern as SC2: the shell pipeline combines retrieval and execution, so users should prefer the package-manager options.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: the description is broad, but it is bounded to Outlit customer intelligence and the skill says not to use Outlit for generic customer-success advice without workspace data.
[EA2] expected: Overridden: the cited text is secret-handling guidance telling the agent not to expose provider secrets in chat or logs; the artifact separately requires explicit user requests for writes and explicit authorization for irreversible merges.
